before: The engine's write of different odd and even pages took `w:evenAndOddHeaders` out of `w:settings` and added it at the end, after members such as `w:compat` and `w:rsids` that follow it in `CT_Settings`, so a second write of the same value moved it.
after: The write puts `w:evenAndOddHeaders` after the last `CT_Settings` member that precedes it, as Protect Document is placed, so a second write of the same value gives the same settings part.
reason: Operations, change messages and the Yjs document format do not change. Only the place of one settings element in the saved file changes; every copy writes it with the same code version, so the copies agree. Checkpoints keep reading the element wherever it stands.
